findings.quote: | A display name is required to join and is written permanently on chain | `join_pool` in `programs/commish/src/lib.rs`; the join button is gated on `canJoin`, false while `nameBytes === 0` |
findings.reality: The website half is correct: `src/app/p/[pool]/page.tsx:231-232` sets `problem` to "Pick a name the others will see" when `nameBytes === 0`, `:238-239` makes `canJoin` false whenever `problem` is set, and `:492` disables the button on it. The program half is not: `join_pool` (`lib.rs:272`) passes `display_name` straight to `init_member` (`lib.rs:1136`), which calls `fixed_bytes` (`state.rs:214-220`) — that only checks `bytes.len() <= N` and zero-pads, so an empty string is accepted on chain. The requirement is a property of this website, not of the program. The same table asserts at line 35 that "The program is permissionless and reachable without this site", so a direct call can join with no name at all.
findings.fix: Split the row: "This site requires a display name to join" (UI gate) and "whatever name is submitted is written permanently on chain" (`fixed_bytes`). Check whether the Privacy page makes the stronger claim too; if it does, it needs the same split.

missingDisclosures: README.md never says the product is devnet-only. `Anchor.toml:14` sets `cluster = "devnet"`; `programs/commish/src/constants.rs:16-17` swaps in devnet USDC `4zMMC9srt5Ri5X14GAgXhaHii3GnPAEERYPJgZJDncDU` behind the `devnet` feature; `src/app/risk/page.tsx:68` says "deployed on Solana devnet"; and `src/app/layout.tsx:78-82` sets `robots: { index: false, follow: false, nocache: true }` with the note "REMOVE BOTH AT MAINNET". A reader of "Buy-ins escrowed on-chain... Last one standing takes the pot" has no way to learn the tokens have no value. LEGAL-REVIEW.md:93-97 treats devnet as the central caveat; README carries none of it.

README.md's Architecture section describes the app as "pool creation, join links, the pick grid, and live pool status". It omits: the entire League Treasurer mode (`src/components/LeaguePanel.tsx`, `src/app/pools/new/page.tsx:94-97`), the public leaderboard (`src/app/leaderboard/page.tsx`, `src/lib/leaderboard.ts`), X account linking (`src/app/api/auth/x/*`, `src/components/XLink.tsx`), Sleeper standings import (`src/lib/sleeper.ts`, `src/app/api/sleeper/route.ts`), and the playable game at `/arcade` (`src/app/arcade/page.tsx`, `src/components/CommishBowl.tsx`, `src/lib/bowl.ts`, `src/lib/chiptune.ts`).

README.md's Architecture calls the server "a thin sync layer that proposes weekly results from public NFL scores." That is `src/app/api/scores/route.ts` only. The server also runs a full OAuth 2 + PKCE flow against X (`src/app/api/auth/x/start/route.ts`, `.../callback/route.ts`), issues and burns wallet-signature nonces (`src/app/api/auth/{pending,bind,identity}/route.ts`), and writes a Cloudflare D1 database that stores wallet↔X-handle pairings (`db/schema.sql` tables `identity`, `nonce`, `standing`; client at `src/lib/d1.ts`). That is a materially different privacy surface from "a thin sync layer".

README.md's "What that has actually been put through" section cites only the 19 LiteSVM tests. It does not mention the web suites: 58 tests across `tests-web/auth-guards.test.ts` (16), `tests-web/bowl.test.ts` (25), `tests-web/chiptune.test.ts` (11) and `tests-web/share-name.test.ts` (6), run by `npm run test:web` (`package.json:9`). `auth-guards.test.ts` in particular covers the X-linking guards the legal pages make claims about.

README.md's trust table row "Strand the money | A deadman switch lets members reclaim their share if the pool is ever abandoned" does not disclose that in a league pool `reclaim_dues` is blocked for a further 30 days past the refund deadline whenever any prize slot is still pending or finalized (`programs/commish/src/lib.rs:820-829`, `PRIZE_CLAIM_GRACE_SECS` at `constants.rs:83`).

brand/README.md's asset table omits `avatar-night.svg` and `avatar-night.png`, both of which `scripts/build-brand.mjs:330` and `:337` emit into `brand/`. It also does not mention `brand/fonts/`, a directory that exists and is empty — worth either documenting or deleting, given the same file says "Anton is gone from the repository" and "There is no font install step any more."

LEGAL-REVIEW.md's fact table does not cover the browser storage the arcade introduced. `src/lib/sfx.ts:23` writes a sound preference to `localStorage` under `commish.sfx`, and `src/components/CommishBowl.tsx:72` writes a longest-run score under `commish.bowl.best` (read at `:171`, written at `:271-273`). The Privacy page's local-storage paragraph (`src/app/privacy/page.tsx:147`) discloses only the wallet adapter's storage, so two keys the site writes are undescribed. Neither carries personal data, but the page's list is presented as complete.

LEGAL-REVIEW.md does not record that the Terms now name a contracting entity. `src/app/terms/page.tsx:33` identifies "HoldFi LLC, a Texas limited liability company, whose registered agent is at 5900 Balcones Dr, STE 100, Austin, TX 78731" as the counterparty. The file's "Positions taken that need a lawyer's eye" section discusses the liability cap and the indemnity without noting who they run against, and COMMISHHANDOFF.md:328 and :378 still assert the founder is operating personally with no entity. Whether the cap, the indemnity and the regulatory-characterisation section read the same way against an LLC is a question for counsel.

LEGAL-REVIEW.md's "Things that are true today and will stop being true" list names `src/app/play/page.tsx` and `src/app/privacy/page.tsx` as the devnet-dependent pages (via `scripts/deploy-mainnet.sh:143-145`, which does name exactly those two — verified). It does not mention `src/app/layout.tsx:78-82`, which suppresses search indexing on the same devnet grounds and is handled by a different script (`scripts/mainnet-cutover.sh`, named at `layout.tsx:81`). Two scripts each own part of the mainnet cutover and the review file only names one.
